newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias creditors set rates on loans.
newsitem.headline: Victorias creditors set rates on loans.

text.p: Philippine sugar miller Victorias Milling Co said on Thursday its creditors agreed to peg its peso-denominated loans based on the 90-day Treasury bill rate plus a spread of three percent.
In a disclosure of the Philippine Stock Exchange, the cash-strapped firm also said its creditors agreed to peg its foreign loans based on the LIBOR rate plus a spread of three percent.
Victorias has obtained a 90-day reprieve on the principal payments of its 4.423 billion pesos in debt.
Victorias said the loan repricing was done at a March 11 meeting with its creditors. The company did not disclose the previous pricing of the loans.
"The concerns of the creditors and the public as well will be best addressed by the due diligence being undertaken by (Philippine accounting firm) Joaquin Cunanan," Victorias said in its statement.
It said the audit is being undertaken preparatory to Victorias' plan to take in "possible strategic partnerships". It did not elaborate.
A committee formed by creditors of Victorias to negotiate directly with the sugar miller asked the firm on Tuesday to speed up the audit to one month from three.
About 10 to 12 banks of the 32 total creditors have collaterals on their loans. Seven foreign banks are also included in the creditor group.
Victorias has assured the creditors committee it has enough funds to pay interests on its debt on March 14.
Of the 4.423 billion pesos debt of Victorias, the bulk of three billion pesos carry a maturity of less than one year.
